Propose exactly 1 DISTINCT, implementable idea for improving the item semantic IDs that a generative recommender consumes. You are one of 5 independent ideation agents: aim for a different part of the design space than the others, and do not copy an existing mechanism in the repository.
THE RESEARCH OBJECTIVE:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.
THE SCOPE CONTRACT (a proposal that misses it is sent back, not scored):
A proposal is IN SCOPE only when all of this holds:
  1. BEHAVIOUR: it names one training-only behaviour signal (directed item transitions, user-interest branching, sequential co-consumption, popularity-adjusted graph neighbours, behaviour-conditioned assignment weights, ...) and says how it is computed.
  2. HYPERBOLIC GEOMETRY: it names an explicit curved operation (trainable or fixed negative curvature, Poincare or Lorentz distance, exp/log maps, geodesic scoring, curved residual, curved quantization, curved regularization) and where in training or quantization it acts.
  3. REAL COUPLING: one connected computational pathway uses both, so that removing either changes the core computation. A behaviour suffix on an unchanged Euclidean quantizer, a standalone hyperbolic loss beside an unrelated behaviour loss, a geometry name without geometric computation, or inherited unused hyperbolic code do NOT qualify.
  4. TESTABLE EFFECT: it states what should observably change (SID assignment, gradient or parameter update, prefix behaviour predictability, or Stage3 Recall) and names the behaviour-off, geometry-off/Euclidean and both-on comparisons. The three switches must be part of the mechanism, so that the coupling can be shown to be real, but the round RUNS no ablation arm: each candidate is trained once.
  5. MINIMAL SPECIFICATION: equations or pseudocode, inputs and outputs, numerical safeguards and the training cost. No proof and no paper section are required.
SID quality (ER, prefix counts, collisions) is NOT a scope criterion and NOT an admission rule.

EXPERIMENT POLICY (binding on every proposal, implementation and review):
  - ONE candidate, ONE training run, on the frozen budget (3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, the frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping).
  - NO ablation experiments: the behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches must EXIST in the code and must be correct, but no arm is trained with them switched off.
  - NO tuning experiments: no sweep over the coupling weight, the clip bound, the temperature, the usage weight or any other constant. A constant that enters the mechanism has to be DERIVED (a scale-relative bound, a measured quantity, a documented default), not chosen by trying values.
  - NO multi-seed experiments: a candidate is not repeated with other seeds, so a single run decides it and the seed noise is part of the uncertainty.
  - The behavioural diagnostics (coherence, adjacency, transfer predictability) are recorded, never used as an admission gate; Stage 3 test_recall@10 is the judgement.
  - A proposal that needs an ablation, a sweep or a seed repetition to make its case is out of programme: it has to make the case with one run.
Explore materially different coupling positions, for example: behaviour-weighted curved assignment or Sinkhorn; behaviour hierarchy in a negatively curved latent or quantizer; behaviour-directed curved residual or transition optimization. These are examples, not a fixed list.

A THIRD exploration of the behaviour-graph curvature, aimed at the two failures the first two rounds measured rather than at a new idea. THE EVIDENCE: (1) The standardised behaviour-graph curvature profile is real and measurable: on the frozen baseline TIGER_RQ-VAE's prefixes the null-standardised Ollivier curvature of the training behaviour quotient graph is kappa_hat = [-2.32, -1.80, -0.86] over the three levels, i.e. the baseline's fine level is LESS curved than its size-preserving null; the mean-zero deviation gives delta = [-0.328, -0.071, +0.399] and a per-level curvature of [1.389, 1.074, 0.671]. The raw curvature is unrelated to the recall (Spearman +0.03, p=0.65) because the level sizes differ; only the standardised value carries a signal (the level-1 minus level-3 deviation tracks the recall at -0.20, p=0.0095 over 115 mechanism families), and it adds only about one percentage point of R^2 on top of the plain SID-quality measures, which is why the round-1 arm spent it on the space's radius, the codebook collapsed from 170 to 56 distinct triples, and Stage3 test_recall@10 came out at 0.041888, BELOW the 0.0446 of the arm it inherited and 36% below the 0.065 target. (2) The machine verification REFUSED the round-2 proposal (CURVCAP-SUCCPLAN) at the launch, and it was right: the behaviour entered as a MULTIPLICATIVE per-pair weight on the cost, and the check measured that the margins moved (two of four by 1.0 and 3.6) while NOT ONE arg-min moved -- a rescaling of a distance can only reorder the nearest code when two codes are almost equidistant, so the coupling cannot be certified as a behaviour dependency. (3) The capacity freeze the round-2 proposal used to protect the resolution is only partial: the arg-max of a plan with fixed column sums need not reproduce those marginals. THIS ROUND's question: what makes the behaviour term a PROVABLE dependency and the resolution protection EXACT? Requirements every proposal must meet, each of which is a measured failure of the previous rounds: (a) ADDITIVITY: the behaviour term must enter the assignment as an ADDITIVE bias on the cost (or an equivalent term whose top-1 effect is provable), not as a multiplicative rescaling of a distance; the machine verification must be able to measure that the top-1 indices change when the behaviour signal is switched off, with the change reported; (b) EXACT RESOLUTION PROTECTION: the per-level usage multiset must be protected BY CONSTRUCTION -- an assignment rule whose output has the Euclidean usage multiset exactly, not a plan whose arg-max may not reproduce its marginals; the proposal must show the construction, not assert it; (c) THE CURVATURE IS SPENT, NOT SHRUNK: whatever the curvature does, it must not act as a scale on the codebook's radius (that is what collapsed the codebook), and if the curvature is not spent at all, the proposal must say why the behaviour-graph curvature is then in the mechanism; (d) the curvature measurement must come from the TRAINING split only, must be standardised against a size-preserving member-shuffle null, and must be measured OFFLINE or on every rank, so that no rank-0-only broadcast or export happens inside the training loop (that deadlock killed three launches of the round-1 arm); (e) the three switches (behaviour off, geometry off/Euclidean, both on) must be part of the mechanism, and only the both-on arm is trained. The frozen baseline TIGER_RQ-VAE (247/7414/20223, Stage3 test_recall@10 0.055537) is the reference, and the numbers to beat are its support and its recall; the first-level hit rates must stay near 0.079/0.005 and the collision near 0.177, not the 0.998/0.982/0.980 of the collapsed arms.
